**2.** Ines is right: recoding the binary predictor as 0/1 makes it numerical, and the resulting correlation coefficient (the point-biserial correlation) is a valid summary of the association.

(b) Essentially no — the small drifts differ by tournament (unpressured shots drift up only at the men's World Cup; both lines drift slightly down at the Women's Euro), but all remain tiny. (c) The faceted plots: competition is a grouping variable, and the combined plot masks the fact that the drifts run in different directions at the two tournaments.

**6.** (a) False — collinear predictors share information, so removing one shifts the point estimate of the other. (b) True. (c) False — the coefficient describes the predicted difference between players who differ by 1 in $x_1$, not the effect of intervening on a player's $x_1$; no individual's observed $y$ is guaranteed to rise by 5.7.
